title: Migrant welfare board cannot cash Tk 564 crore stuck in merged bank
excerpt: The Wage Earners' Welfare Board says matured deposits held by Sammilito Islami Bank are holding up services for migrant workers' families.

image.alt: Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka at dusk
image.credit: Md Shaifuzzaman Ayon / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0

content:
The Wage Earners' Welfare Board (WEWB) cannot cash Tk 5.64 billion (Tk 564 crore) of matured fixed deposits now held by the merged Sammilito Islami Bank, and has asked the government to step in, The Financial Express reported on Wednesday (18 November).

The deposits were placed with four of the banks merged into Sammilito Islami Bank: First Security Islami Bank (Tk 4.45 billion), Union Bank (Tk 1.05 billion), Global Islami Bank (Tk 130 million) and Exim Bank (Tk 10 million).

The board says the frozen money is hampering welfare services for migrant workers and their families. The Financial Institutions Division said it is working to resolve the issue, the report said. No officials were named.

Why it matters

The board pays for services such as grants, medical and legal aid, stipends and the repatriation of migrants' bodies. Organisations working with migrants will see the effect if payments slow.

What to watch

Whether the Financial Institutions Division releases the money, and whether any WEWB services are delayed or cut in the meantime.
